data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject when the test's own existence changes what the subject is allowed to be, and it describes the subject when the test is a by-product of the subject's construction; the 3-of-26 result is a consequence of the fact that the three survivors are one bug in two costumes, where the guard checks declared data but not added behavior.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the test were written to fail when the subject's behavior changes, the three survivors would be caught.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the guard were extended to check added behavior, the distribution would shift.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the mutation changed declared data, the guard would catch it and the test would constrain the subject.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The test constrains by acting as a normative boundary that the subject must respect. When the test only verifies properties that the subject already has by construction, it is redundant and describes rather than constrains.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
